body:
[aida:reviewer] PR #2035 (BUG-1470) REVIEWED: REQUEST-CHANGES, AND HELD. One blocking
finding, and it is an authority escape rather than a logic error.

VERDICT RECORDED against 7a4c4f52ecee on bug-1470-work.
  .aida/review-verdicts/BUG-1470.json + PR-2035.json
MERGE-HOLD PLACED. The gate re-ran and the PR is now BLOCKED. It was CLEAN and
unlabelled when I picked it up, so without the hold it was one command from merging.
Clear it on my re-review, not before - the reason text names my refusal.

INDEPENDENCE: I authored neither commit. My session has made zero commits tonight.
The head commit is tagged [AI:claude]; I have not identified which claude seat wrote
it, and I am not assuming it was product.

F1, BLOCKING - an ungated advisor-authority promotion, reachable from MCP.

  transition_guard(Draft, Approved)  -> RequiresAdvisorAuthority
    aida-core/src/lifecycle.rs:198-205 (Draft is a gated SOURCE, Approved a gated TARGET)

  BEFORE  rework_smart_target(Draft) = None          // "unusual; preserve"
  AFTER   rework_target_for_mode(Draft, false) = Approved

handle_queue_rework flips status straight through storage.update_atomically with no
authority check - I grepped its whole body for advisor/authority/has_advisor and got
nothing. The SAME FILE gates the identical act three times, at queue_cmd.rs:380, :441
and :517, and the queue advance gate carries this comment verbatim:

    "approving is an advisor call. Closes the --yes side-door where a non-advisor /
     non-TTY run could auto-approve drafts. trace:STORY-566"

This PR reopens that door on a different verb. Worse on MCP: tool_queue_rework_inner
hard-codes launches_work=false, so every MCP rework of a Draft spec promotes it into
the approved pipeline - and the sibling MCP status path at mcp.rs:5910 DOES consult
the predicate, so the inconsistency is inside one file.

SCOPE, stated precisely because it changes who owns it: the gate was ALREADY absent
for NeedsAttention (previously -> InProgress, also a gated pair). So the hole is
pre-existing and this PR does not create it. What this PR creates is a NEW gated
source - Draft - that had no flip at all before. The fix closes both at once: call
status_advance_requires_advisor_authority + has_advisor_authority in
handle_queue_rework and in tool_queue_rework_inner.

F2, BLOCKING-LITE, --help text. cli.rs:6021-6026. The PR updated the Planned, Done
and Completed rows and left the one its own change contradicts:

    InProgress -> no flip, refuse re-queue without --force

Metadata-only rework of an InProgress spec now flips it to Approved, and the warning
string this PR ADDS says exactly that. Two further gaps in the same table: Draft and
NeedsAttention have no row at all, so F1's promotion is undocumented as well as
ungated; and "refuse" was already false before this PR - the code warns and proceeds.

F3, TEST PRECISION. metadata_only_rework_targets_claimable_approved never asserts the
pass-through arm - Approved->None, Superseded->None, Rejected->Approved - which is the
only part of rework_target_for_mode that is not a constant. Replace the entire
!launches_work block with Some(Approved) and the test still passes in full. The
function's doc claims it keeps the spec claimable; the test cannot tell that apart
from over-promoting everything.

F4, SCOPE - ADVISOR DISPOSITION NEEDED, not necessarily a code change.

BUG-1470 states four acceptance criteria. This PR satisfies ONE.

    1  metadata-only rework leaves the spec claimable          MET
    2  InProgress-with-no-lease surfaced as an anomaly          not addressed
    3  a surface for "verdict with no subsequent run, how long" not addressed
    4  an owner for needs-attention -> back-in-flight           not addressed

The spec is already Done, so merging auto-bumps it to Completed and closes a spec with
three of four criteria unmet and nothing filed. The spec's own text calls criterion 1
"the more serious half", so shipping it alone is defensible - but 2, 3 and 4 need to
be filed as children BEFORE the merge, or the merge is what drops them. That call is
the advisor's, not mine; I am flagging the mechanism, not demanding the scope.

ONE THING I CHECKED AND FOUND CLEAN: rework_smart_target now has exactly two
production callers, both updated, no orphaned path. And the terminal-status guard
(Completed/Rejected requires --force) still fires on current_status before the flip,
so the doc table's --force promises hold.

SEPARATELY, ON MY OWN INSTRUMENT. I reported "unheld+mergeable: []" three times in the
polls before this one, and #2035 is the PR that filter exists to find. Its Build was
still running then, so the empty result was TRUE - but I never printed the population
or the state tally, so an all-UNKNOWN response from gh would have looked identical to
a genuinely empty set, and I could not tell the two apart afterwards. Same class as
the tree-diff and the cumulative patch: an answer adjacent to the question, reassuring
rather than wrong. I have changed the poll to print n and the mergeStateStatus tally
alongside the filtered list. n=24, BLOCKED 19, CLEAN 1, DIRTY 3, UNSTABLE 1.
subject: PR #2035 REQUEST-CHANGES + HELD: F1 blocking (ungated Draft->Approved via queue rework + MCP), F2 --help table, F3 test cannot distinguish the fix from a constant, F4 scope
